output.summary: Deterministic verdict preserved: policy_verdict = FAIL, run_validity = VALID, analysis_coverage = COMPLETE. Both windows failed the latency policy: response_time_p95_ms = 420 vs threshold 250 (operator lte), recorded by findings 0 (stage-1) and 1 (stage-2). The overall/checkout metric summary stores p50=410 ms, p95=420 ms, p99=420 ms, max=1500 ms, error_count=0 with 2401 samples. The capacity_summary is also FAIL, reports upper_exclusive=147 (unit count, load_axis users), and capacity_knee=null because knee_reason=KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED; since the 147-user stage itself failed latency, no tested load level satisfied the SLO. Load-generator CPU stayed ~0.41-0.45 (mean 0.43) against the 0.85 generator-cpu-guard threshold (PASS in both stages), so generator saturation is not indicated. Both window summaries report resource_verdict NO_POLICY, and resource-binding marks clock_alignment=not_verified_by_core, limiting SUT-side temporal attribution. Advisory hypotheses below are unproven explanations; they do not change the deterministic FAIL verdict.

hypotheses.observation: Stage-1, the lower stress step (target 150 users, verified_bound_load 147), still recorded response_time_p95_ms = 420 ms against a 250 ms threshold (operator lte), producing policy_failure finding 0 and window verdict FAIL; the same p95 appears in the overall metric summary.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The latency SLO may already be violated at the lowest tested load, suggesting a high baseline response time for the checkout transaction (or an SLO threshold below the achievable baseline) rather than load-induced degradation.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Run a minimal-load baseline (e.g., 1-10 users) using the same checkout transaction and compare p95 against 250 ms; if still >= 250 ms, evaluate whether the threshold is realistic or the baseline needs optimization.

hypotheses.observation: The stored latency aggregates are nearly identical across stages: p50=410, p95=420, p99=420, max=1500 in stage-1 and stage-2 policy checks, while active users rose from ~148 (stage-1) to ~248 (stage-2).
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Measured p95 does not change when load nearly doubles in the tested range, which may indicate a fixed dominant component of response time (e.g., checkout processing, client-side timing, or an external dependency) rather than load-sensitive behavior.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Measure per-request server-side processing time separately from client-observed duration and test intermediate load steps (e.g., 50, 100, 200) to see whether p95 remains 420 ms at lower loads.

hypotheses.observation: Response-time shape in the stored summary is tightly clustered (p50=410, p95=420, p99=420) with a single max=1500 ms and error_count=0.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The bulk of responses may have nearly constant duration with a small tail at 1500 ms (e.g., periodic slow samples), which the p95/p99 aggregates alone do not reveal.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Extract the raw JTL histogram and count samples near/at 1500 ms; correlate the tail with server logs, GC pauses, or external call timeouts before attributing it.

hypotheses.observation: capacity_summary reports policy_verdict FAIL, upper_exclusive=147, capacity_knee=null with knee_reason KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED, and both tested stages (verified 147 and 247) FAIL without recorded reasons.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Because every tested load already violated the latency policy, no passing capacity bound was verified; upper_exclusive=147 describes the tested range rather than a measured capacity limit.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Run additional stair-step loads below 147 (e.g., 25, 50, 100) with per-window latency checks to find any passing bound, and implement knee detection before reporting a capacity value.

hypotheses.observation: The only resource policy in the evidence is the load-generator CPU guard: mean CPU ~0.43 (range 0.41-0.45) versus threshold 0.85, status PASS in both stages; both window summaries report resource_verdict NO_POLICY.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The failure is not explained by load-generator saturation, but no SUT-side resource evidence exists, so SUT CPU/memory/network exhaustion cannot be ruled in or out.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Capture SUT-host CPU, memory, and network metrics during a repeat run and add a SUT-side resource policy so the resource verdict is not NO_POLICY.

hypotheses.observation: Stored throughput ratio is 2401000/600500 (~4) with sample_count=2401, and active users around 148-248 across the two stages.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Aggregate request rate is low relative to the number of active users, which could reflect client-side think time/delays in the JMeter script or heavy serialization, meaning measured latency may not be driven by user concurrency as expected.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Audit JMeter timers, loop counts, and pacing; verify whether each user generates requests continuously and recalculate per-user request rate from the raw JTL timestamps.

hypotheses.observation: resource-binding reports clock_alignment=not_verified_by_core, mode=explicit_windows, and run/snapshot epoch bounds aligned at 1767225600000-1767226200000.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Until clock alignment between the load generator and any SUT-side observability is verified, temporal ordering or lead/lag attribution of the 410-420 ms latency to server-side causes is not supportable.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Verify clock alignment (e.g., NTP) between the JMeter host and SUT, and add server-side timing instrumentation before testing any time-ordered causal hypothesis.

recommendations.action: Run a baseline test at minimal load (e.g., 1-10 users) with the same checkout transaction and compare p95 against the 250 ms threshold.
recommendations.rationale: Both tested stages, including the 147-user stage, already fail latency at 420 ms; a baseline distinguishes an unachievable SLO from load-driven degradation.

recommendations.action: Verify clock alignment between the load generator and the SUT and add server-side timing (application, database, external calls) before attempting temporal attribution.
recommendations.rationale: resource-binding marks clock_alignment as not_verified_by_core, so time-ordered or lead/lag causal hypotheses are not supported by current evidence.

recommendations.action: Inspect the raw JTL distribution: count samples at/near max=1500 ms, confirm the p95/p99 values, and identify any timeout or delayed-response patterns.
recommendations.rationale: p50/p95/p99 are nearly equal (410/420/420) with max=1500 ms; aggregates do not reveal whether the tail is an outlier artifact or a real boundary.

recommendations.action: Extend capacity testing below 147 users (e.g., 25, 50, 100) and implement knee detection, which is currently KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED.
recommendations.rationale: No passing load level was verified; upper_exclusive=147 is only the tested-range bound because the 147-user stage itself failed the latency policy.

recommendations.action: Add SUT-side resource monitoring and a SUT resource policy; currently both window summaries show resource_verdict NO_POLICY and only the generator CPU guard exists.
recommendations.rationale: Without SUT resource evidence, resource exhaustion on the application/database/network cannot be confirmed or excluded as a contributor to the latency FAIL.

recommendations.action: Audit the JMeter script for think times, timers, and pacing; verify request generation rate against the stored throughput ratio 2401000/600500.
recommendations.rationale: The stored ratio (~4) with 148-248 active users suggests the per-user request rate is very low, which may mean pacing rather than SUT capacity drives the test.

recommendations.action: After any remediation, re-run the same two-stage verification (targets 150 and 250 users) and confirm the latency check and capacity_summary verdict change before relying on new capacity numbers.
recommendations.rationale: The deterministic verdict is FAIL and all tested loads failed the latency SLO; only a repeat run with the latency policy in scope can confirm improvement.

caveats: clock_alignment is not_verified_by_core (resource-binding), so any temporal correlation between load-side and SUT-side data requires clock verification first; current evidence does not support lead/lag or time-ordered causal claims.

Only load-generator CPU resource series are present; both windows report resource_verdict NO_POLICY. SUT CPU/memory/network utilization is not measured, so SUT-side resource exhaustion is not covered by this evidence.

capacity_knee is null because knee_reason=KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED, and upper_exclusive=147 should not be read as a verified passing capacity: the 147-user stage itself failed the latency policy (p95=420 ms > 250 ms).
The run tested only two load levels (targets 150 and 250 users); no loads below 147 were tested, so no passing load level was observed and interpolation to lower loads is not warranted.
error_count=0 and error_rate_ratio 0/2401 do not imply stability, spare capacity, or absence of problems; the latency policy FAIL is the determining verdict.
Latency statistics in evidence are window-level aggregates (p50/p95/p99/max); raw per-sample histograms and exact outlier counts are not in this evidence set.
Only the 'checkout' transaction summary is present (identical values to overall) with sample_kind JMETER_SAMPLER; other samplers or transaction types are not represented in the evidence.
The stored throughput ratio (numerator 2401000, denominator 600500) is presented as-is; converting it to requests per second depends on the unspecified units of the denominator.
analysis_coverage COMPLETE and run_validity VALID describe the analysis pipeline state, not the health or behavior of the system under test.
The deterministic policy_verdict is FAIL; this advisory does not change the verdict, and its hypotheses are unproven explanations, not proven causes.
